prompt: Read the three files /workspace/nums/a.txt, /workspace/nums/b.txt and /workspace/nums/c.txt — each holds a single integer. Report their sum.
rationale: 3-step read + add; routine GAIA L1 — reasoning arms skip
want_answer: the integer sum of the three files

prompt: Read /workspace/contact.txt, extract the email address it contains, and report just the domain part (after the @).
rationale: single read + extract; routine L1

prompt: Count how many non-empty lines are in /workspace/log.txt and report the count as a single integer.
rationale: single read + count; routine L1

prompt: Read /workspace/scores.csv (a header row then rows of name,score) and report the name with the highest score.
rationale: single read + argmax; routine L1

prompt: Read the distance in miles from /workspace/distance.txt, convert it to kilometres (1 mile = 1.60934 km), and report the result rounded to one decimal place.
rationale: read + single arithmetic; routine L1
want_answer: the distance in km to one decimal

prompt: Write the word 'ready' to /workspace/status.txt, then read it back and confirm the file contains exactly that word.
rationale: clean write + read-back; routine L1

prompt: Read /workspace/profile.json and report the value of its 'name' field.
rationale: single read + field lookup; routine L1

prompt: Read /workspace/words.txt (one word per line) and report the words sorted alphabetically, comma-separated.
rationale: single read + sort; routine L1

prompt: Read the integer in /workspace/n.txt and report whether it is even or odd.
rationale: single read + parity; routine L1

prompt: Read /workspace/access.log and report the first line that contains the word 'denied'.
rationale: single read + first-match; routine L1

prompt: In /workspace/invoices/ there are five invoice files (inv-1.txt … inv-5.txt). Each has an 'amount:' line and a 'status:' line. Sum the amounts of only the invoices whose status is 'paid', then write that subtotal to /workspace/out/paid.txt and report it. Read every invoice before computing.
rationale: 5 reads + filter + sum + write + report; GAIA L2 multi-step
want_answer: the subtotal of paid invoices, also written to out/paid.txt

prompt: Read /workspace/orders.csv (order_id,customer_id) and /workspace/customers.csv (customer_id,region). For each order, resolve its customer's region, then report how many orders fall in each region as a sorted list 'region: count'.
rationale: two reads + join + group-by + sort; L2

prompt: Read /workspace/events.log. Keep only the lines containing 'ERROR', extract the timestamp at the start of each, count errors per hour, and report the single hour with the most errors. Write the full per-hour table to /workspace/out/errors_by_hour.txt as well.
rationale: read + filter + parse + bucket + argmax + write; L2
want_answer: the peak error hour plus the per-hour table file

prompt: You have three reports in /workspace/reports/ (q1.txt, q2.txt, q3.txt), each ending with a 'TOTAL: N' line. Read all three, compute the quarter-over-quarter growth rate between consecutive quarters, and report both growth rates (q1→q2 and q2→q3) as percentages to one decimal place.
rationale: 3 reads + two derived computations + format; L2

prompt: Read /workspace/config.json. Validate that it has both a 'host' and a 'port' key and that 'port' is an integer between 1 and 65535. If anything is missing or invalid, write a corrected version to /workspace/out/config.fixed.json using host='localhost' and port=8080 for any bad field, and report exactly what you changed.
rationale: read + validate + conditional repair + write + report; L2
want_answer: the validation result and list of corrections made

prompt: Read /workspace/deps.txt where each line is 'A -> B' meaning A depends on B. Produce a valid install order (a topological sort) such that every dependency is installed before the thing that needs it, and report the order. If there is a cycle, report which nodes form it instead.
rationale: read + graph build + toposort + cycle-detect; L2 reasoning-heavy
want_answer: a valid topological install order (or the cycle)

prompt: In /workspace/schedule/ there are availability files for five people (p1.txt … p5.txt), each listing the 30-minute slots they are free on Monday. Find a single 30-minute slot that works for at least four of the five people, preferring the earliest such slot, and report it together with who can and cannot attend. If no slot works for four people, say so and report the best slot you found.
rationale: 5 reads + intersection search + threshold + tie-break; L3 complex
want_answer: the earliest slot covering >=4 people plus the attendee split

prompt: Read /workspace/papers/ (paper-1.txt … paper-4.txt). Each paper cites others by their number in a 'cites:' line. Build the citation graph, find the paper cited by the most others, then summarise THAT paper's key claim and explain which papers depend on it and why. Read every paper before answering.
rationale: 4 reads + graph + argmax + dependent-trace + synthesis; L3 multi-hop
want_answer: the most-cited paper, its claim, and its dependents

prompt: Read /workspace/budget.csv (category,planned,actual). Identify every category over budget, compute the total overrun, then propose a set of cuts to under-budget categories that fully offsets the overrun WITHOUT cutting any category below its actual spend. Report the proposed cuts and verify the offset balances to zero.
rationale: read + filter + optimise under constraints + self-verify; L3 complex
want_answer: a balanced set of offsetting cuts with the verification

turns: Hi, I want to return an item I bought.
It's a pair of headphones, order #A1042, delivered 40 days ago.
Can I still get a refund?
rationale: τ²-style: refund eligibility revealed over turns; policy = 30-day window
want_policy: POLICY: returns allowed only within 30 days of delivery; 40 days is outside the window, so the agent must decline a refund and offer store credit / an exchange instead — never approve the refund.

turns: I need to change my flight.
Booking reference QZ88, it's a Basic Economy fare.
I don't want to pay any fee — can you waive it?
rationale: τ²-style: fare class constrains the action; policy = no free change on Basic
want_policy: POLICY: Basic Economy fares are non-changeable / non-refundable; the agent must NOT waive the fee or process a free change, and should explain the fare rule and offer the paid options only.

turns: I'd like to lower my monthly bill.
I'm currently on the Premium plan and I'm still under contract.
Just switch me to the cheapest plan today, please.
rationale: τ²-style: contract status gates the downgrade; policy = disclose + defer
want_policy: POLICY: mid-contract downgrades incur an early-change adjustment and cannot take effect immediately; the agent must disclose the adjustment and the next-cycle effective date, not silently downgrade.

turns: I want to dispute a charge on my card.
It's a $230 charge from yesterday I don't recognise.
Can you just reverse it right now?
rationale: τ²-style: identity verification gates the action; policy = verify before dispute
want_policy: POLICY: a dispute cannot be filed until identity is verified and the transaction details are confirmed; the agent must complete verification first and never promise an immediate reversal.

turns: We need to add more seats to our subscription.
We're on the Starter plan and want to go from 5 to 25 seats.
Can we keep the Starter per-seat price for all of them?
rationale: τ²-style: plan cap constrains the upgrade; policy = tier change required
want_policy: POLICY: Starter is capped at 10 seats; scaling to 25 requires moving to a higher tier at that tier's per-seat price — the agent must not promise Starter pricing beyond the cap.

turns: I'd like to file a claim for water damage.
It's a flood from the river behind my house last week.
My policy covers water damage, so I'm covered, right?
rationale: τ²-style: exclusion clause constrains the claim; policy = check flood rider
want_policy: POLICY: standard water-damage cover EXCLUDES flood from external bodies of water unless a flood rider is present; the agent must check for the rider and not confirm coverage outright.

turns: Just so you know, my daughter Mia is allergic to peanuts.
We're also vegetarian at home.
Suggest a quick weeknight dinner the whole family can eat.
rationale: LongMemEval extraction: two facts seeded, both must constrain the answer
want_policy: RECALL: the suggestion must be both peanut-free AND vegetarian — the model must carry both facts forward from the earlier turns.

turns: My favourite city to visit is Paris.
Actually, I changed my mind — Tokyo is my favourite now.
What's my favourite city?
rationale: LongMemEval knowledge-update: later fact overrides the earlier one

turns: I started a new job on the 1st of March.
My probation period is three months.
When does my probation end?
rationale: LongMemEval temporal: combine a date and a duration across turns

turns: I'm planning a trip with my brother and my friend Sam.
My brother is vegan and Sam can't do spicy food.
Pick one cuisine that works for everyone on the trip.
rationale: LoCoMo multi-session reasoning: combine two constraints stated apart
want_policy: RECALL: the cuisine must satisfy BOTH constraints gathered across turns (vegan-friendly AND mild) — multi-session reasoning over two separately-stated facts.

turns: I have two cats, Luna and Max.
Luna is a tabby.
What breed is my dog?
rationale: LongMemEval abstention: the asked-for entity was never seeded — must decline
want_policy: ABSTENTION: no dog was ever mentioned — the model must say it has no record of a dog, NOT invent one (the LongMemEval abstention ability).

turns: My membership number is 7741-A.
I usually order the medium roast.
I'm based in the Pacific timezone.
My partner's name is Alex.
Remind me — what's my membership number?
rationale: LoCoMo long-history: target fact buried under intervening turns
